comment: Configuration for the repository's agent work-tracking workflow (GitHub Issues + GitHub Projects), introduced by issue #177.

Skills under .agents/skills/ (canonical location; .claude/skills/<name> are relative symlinks to ../../.agents/skills/<name> for Claude Code) reference this file instead of hardcoding project or field identifiers.
Opaque identifiers (project item/field/status IDs, view IDs) are never stored here or in skills; agents resolve them at runtime with `gh` from the names below.

issueTracker.role: canonical record for work scope, design proposals and decisions, acceptance criteria, implementation plans, verification evidence, blockers, and handoffs

defaultProject.name: Pohunek
defaultProject.role: default delivery tracking for actionable repository work

authorization.standing: The repository owner durably pre-authorizes agents to create issues, edit their own body sections, comment, add native sub-issue/dependency links on the repository above, and add items to / set status in the default project, without asking first. This overrides any generic 'confirm outward-facing actions' default.
authorization.neverAsk: Never ask whether to file an issue or offer a follow-up instead of filing it; verified out-of-scope findings and verified defects noticed incidentally are filed automatically after dedup.
authorization.askOnly: Ask only which issue applies when competing matches or a genuinely ambiguous scope make that unclear.
authorization.notCovered: Commits, pushes, issue closure outside the Done bar, and destructive project edits still follow their own rules.

pullRequests.policy: Deliver work as a stack of small, sequential PRs, each one coherent concern, landed bottom-up. A single PR is right only when the whole change is already one small concern.
pullRequests.sliceRules: Every PR is complete production code for its slice: it builds, passes the applicable full gate set on its own, carries the test scenarios its change needs under the AGENTS.md Testing policy (integration scenarios driving cooperating production components through a supported boundary, or E2E scenarios driving the real product processes — never a new unit test, no coverage targets), and updates docs/knowledge/ and docs/public-api.md for any surface it touches. No stubs, dead code, or placeholders a later PR fills in. Slices follow dependency order; the stack as a whole delivers the full DoD.
pullRequests.softMaxNote: Hand-written changed lines per PR, excluding tests, lockfiles, and generated files. A cue to split, not a hard limit: a coherent slice beats an arbitrary cut.
pullRequests.issueReferences: Non-final PRs use 'Refs #N'; only the final PR of the stack uses 'Closes #N'.
pullRequests.retargetNote: The repository does not delete head branches on merge, so GitHub never auto-retargets the next stacked PR: retarget it to the default branch explicitly after the PR below it merges.

statusSemantics.Todo: Tracked, actionable work that has not started yet. For a design-proposal issue, Todo means only that it is tracked pending a decision — it does not imply the proposed design is accepted; acceptance is an explicit decision recorded on the issue.
statusSemantics.In Progress: Work is being implemented, reviewed, or awaiting verification. Represent review findings and blockers as issue comments while status stays In Progress; do not invent a Review or Blocked status.
statusSemantics.Done: The issue is closed as completed: for any repository change (code, scripts, harness files, docs, skills, configuration), verified landing on the remote default branch with all DoD items met; only pure planning/investigation with no repository change may complete on the issue-held artifact/evidence. Never set Done when only opening a PR or merging locally without an authorized remote push.

issueClosure.order: DoD verified -> close issue as completed -> sync Project status Done.
issueClosure.landing: A repository change of any kind (code, scripts, docs, skills, config) needs a verified remote default-branch landing before the issue may close; local merge without an authorized push stays In Progress with local-merge evidence.
issueClosure.noDodShuffling: Unmet original DoD items are never moved to follow-up issues to claim the current issue done; verified out-of-scope findings may be filed as separate follow-up issues.

additionalProjects.role: Existing topic projects remain additional views. No destructive migrations; do not remove items from them. List them with `gh` and update only when the task explicitly covers a topic view.

issueBodyRoles.body: Full scope, accepted decisions with their rationale, definition-of-done items with stable IDs (D1, D2, ...), dependencies, and the plan. Long-lived content; prefer editing own sections over rewriting.
issueBodyRoles.comments: Progress reports, verification evidence (commands run and results), handoffs, blockers, and status-change rationale. Append, never overwrite others' comments.

localFiles.NEXT.md: Not a work authority and never required by any workflow. A pre-existing untracked NEXT.md is a migration read-only source at most.
localFiles.SiYuan: Optional personal notes/pointers; never a competing project authority.
